title: Add RAG SparkNotebook: lightweight in-notebook RAG workshop and samples
author: Maya Patel
description: Introduce a compact, hands-on RAG workshop delivered as a SparkNotebook (lightweight notebook format) aimed at developer onboarding and iterative authoring. Motivation: many users want a single-file, offline-friendly lab that demonstrates incremental indexing, prefix caching behavior, and step checkpoints for RAG workflows without spinning up a full dev server. This PR adds a curated quickstart that: 1) demonstrates ingesting a small corpus and building an incremental index with a local WASM retrieval adapter; 2) shows live KV prefix caching effects and how batching/sequence-length settings change cost and latency; 3) includes a checkpointed step runner so authors can resume midway and assert expected outputs; 4) wires lightweight telemetry probes (token counts, latency histograms, hit/miss rates) that map to the Console ingest events for easier mapping to production metrics. Change summary: added a new quickstart under docs/quickstarts/rag-sparknotebook with a SparkNotebook README and three runnable notebook cells (indexing, query loop, evaluate/assert). Included a tiny JS WASM adapter shim for local retrieval use in the notebook and a minimal auth stub for safe local runs. Also added a short developer guide page to the docs site explaining mappings between the notebook probes and Redwood Console dashboards. Checklist: - [x] Add workshop notebook and README - [x] Add WASM retrieval adapter shim and auth stub - [x] Add docs site guide and example screenshots - [x] Add automated smoke test in CI to run the notebook headless and verify example assertions - [x] Add note about safe defaults (no keys, canned demo data) Testing: unit tests for the adapter shim, CI headless run of the notebook with playwright-node runner to ensure assertions pass, manual validation of Console telemetry mapping. Related: references ENG-1987 for telemetry UX improvements and SUP-3321 for a customer request for low-friction dev labs. How to try: clone repo, open docs/quickstarts/rag-sparknotebook/WORKSHOP.sparknb in SparkNotebook viewer or run headless: tools/notebook-runner --file WORKSHOP.sparknb --headless. Security: notebook uses canned demo data by default and the auth stub intentionally rejects networked KMS calls; docs include an explicit section on converting the example to use customer keys. Rollout: this is docs/examples only, no runtime changes. Release notes: Adds a new interactive quickstart (RAG SparkNotebook) for hands-on developer onboarding and telemetry mapping. Reviewer notes: kept code samples small and dependency-free to minimize maintenance surface.
